title: Casting character voices in plain text, generated locally with Ming-3.0 TTS
author: She3k_JL
selftext:
This voice studio treats casting as a text problem: one box for who the character is, one box for what they say. Three takes from the video, all using AntLing's Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B:

\- "A polite, precise, slightly robotic British butler." says "Good evening. I have tidied your desktop, alphabetized your snacks, and quietly judged your browser history." (7.6 s of speech, made in 3.1 s)

\- "A sweet, slightly shaky elderly grandmother with a mischievous streak." says "Oh sweetheart, I made cookies. Don't tell your mother, but I put extra chocolate in them." (6.2 s, made in 2.5 s)

\- "A dramatic, booming, very deep movie trailer narrator." says "In a world where every computer could talk, one little box dared to whisper." (4.9 s, made in 2.0 s)

Each take has Keep this voice and Another take buttons, and a voice cloned from a 7-second recording joins the cast beside the built-in voices. The panel carries presets for a pirate captain, a noir detective and a news anchor, tags like sigh, cough and uhm, emotion buttons, and speed and pitch controls.

For a game, set up a dialogue table with columns for character description, line, emotion and speed. Generate every row, audition a second take where a line falls flat, and keep the voices you like.
